name: numeric
description: Number theory, exact rounding modes, primes, combinatorics and statistics for Int, F64 and BigInt, pure and tested in both tiers

api.name: int_max
api.doc: The largest Int, 2^63 - 1.

api.name: int_min
api.doc: The smallest Int, -2^63.

api.name: checked_abs
api.doc: The absolute value of `x`, or `none` for `int_min()`, whose absolute value is not an Int.

api.name: sign_int
api.doc: The sign of `x`: -1, 0 or 1.

api.name: sign_f64
api.doc: The sign of `x`: -1.0, 1.0, or `x` itself for zeros (keeping -0.0) and NaN.

api.name: gcd_all
api.doc:
The greatest common divisor of every number in `xs`, never negative; 0 for an empty list or
all zeros. Traps, like `Int.gcd`, only when the result would be 2^63 (only `int_min()` and zeros).

api.name: checked_lcm
api.sig: fn checked_lcm(a: Int, b: Int) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc:
The least common multiple of `a` and `b`, never negative (0 if either is 0), or `none` when
it doesn't fit in an Int.

api.name: lcm_all
api.doc:
The least common multiple of every number in `xs`, never negative: 1 for an empty list, 0
if any is 0, `none` when it doesn't fit in an Int.

api.name: egcd
api.doc:
The extended Euclidean algorithm: `(g, x, y)` with `g = gcd(a, b) >= 0` and
`a * x + b * y == g`. Neither argument may be `int_min()`.

api.name: is_coprime
api.sig: fn is_coprime(a: Int, b: Int) -> Bool
api.doc: Whether `a` and `b` have no common divisor above 1.

api.name: floor_div
api.sig: fn floor_div(a: Int, b: Int where _ != 0) -> Int
api.doc:
Division rounded toward negative infinity, like Python's `//`: `floor_div(-7, 2) == -4`.
Traps on `int_min() / -1`, like `/`.

api.name: floor_mod
api.sig: fn floor_mod(a: Int, b: Int where _ != 0) -> Int
api.doc:
The remainder that goes with `floor_div`, with the sign of `b`, like Python's `%`:
`floor_mod(-7, 2) == 1`, `floor_mod(7, -2) == -1`.

api.name: ceil_div
api.sig: fn ceil_div(a: Int, b: Int where _ != 0) -> Int
api.doc: Division rounded toward positive infinity: `ceil_div(7, 2) == 4`, `ceil_div(-7, 2) == -3`.

api.name: euclid_mod
api.sig: fn euclid_mod(a: Int, b: Int where _ != 0) -> Int
api.doc:
The Euclidean remainder: always in `0 .. |b|`, whatever the signs: `euclid_mod(-7, 3) == 2`.
This is the "mod that is never negative".

api.name: euclid_div
api.sig: fn euclid_div(a: Int, b: Int where _ != 0) -> Int
api.doc: The Euclidean quotient: `a == b * euclid_div(a, b) + euclid_mod(a, b)`.

api.name: addmod
api.sig: fn addmod(a: Int, b: Int, m: Int where _ > 0) -> Int
api.doc: `(a + b) mod m` in `0 .. m`, without overflow for any Int inputs.

api.name: mulmod
api.sig: fn mulmod(a: Int, b: Int, m: Int where _ > 0) -> Int
api.doc:
`(a * b) mod m` in `0 .. m`, without overflow for any Int inputs (it uses BigInt when the
product doesn't fit).

api.name: mod_pow
api.sig: fn mod_pow(base: Int, exp: Int where _ >= 0, m: Int where _ > 0) -> Int
api.doc: `base ^ exp mod m` in `0 .. m`, by square and multiply; `mod_pow(x, 0, m)` is `1 mod m`.

api.name: mod_inv
api.sig: fn mod_inv(a: Int, m: Int where _ > 0) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc:
The inverse of `a` modulo `m`: `x` in `0 .. m` with `a * x mod m == 1 mod m`, or `none`
when `a` and `m` are not coprime.

api.name: isqrt
api.doc: The integer square root: the largest `r` with `r * r <= n`.

api.name: iroot
api.sig: fn iroot(n: Int where _ >= 0, k: Int where _ >= 1) -> Int
api.doc: The integer `k`-th root: the largest `r >= 0` with `r ^ k <= n`.

api.name: icbrt
api.doc:
The integer cube root, rounded toward negative infinity, for any `n`:
`icbrt(27) == 3`, `icbrt(26) == 2`, `icbrt(-9) == -3`.

api.name: checked_pow
api.sig: fn checked_pow(base: Int, exp: Int where _ >= 0) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc:
`base ^ exp`, or `none` if it overflows. `checked_pow(0, 0) == some(1)`.
For exact big powers use `big(base).pow(exp)`.

api.name: is_perfect_square
api.doc: Whether `n` is the square of an Int (0 and 1 are; negatives are not).

api.name: perfect_power
api.doc:
The largest exponent `k >= 2` and its base `b` with `b ^ k == n`, or `none`. Negative `n`
can only be odd powers (`-8` is `(-2, 3)`); 0, 1 and -1 give `none`, since every exponent fits.

api.name: is_perfect_power
api.doc: Whether `n` is `b ^ k` for some Int `b` and `k >= 2` (see `perfect_power`).

api.name: is_power_of_two
api.doc: Whether `n` is a positive power of two (1, 2, 4, ...).

api.name: next_power_of_two
api.doc: The smallest power of two `>= n` (1 for `n <= 1`), or `none` above 2^62.

api.name: digits
api.sig: fn digits(n: Int, base: Int where _ >= 2) -> List[Int]
api.doc: The digits of `|n|` in `base`, most significant first; `[0]` for 0. Works for `int_min()`.

api.name: digit_sum
api.doc: The sum of the decimal digits of `|n|`.

api.name: num_digits
api.sig: fn num_digits(n: Int, base: Int where _ >= 2) -> Int
api.doc: The number of digits of `|n|` in `base` (1 for 0).

api.name: digital_root
api.doc: The repeated digit sum of `|n|` down to one decimal digit (0 for 0, else 1 to 9).

api.name: from_digits
api.sig: fn from_digits(ds: List[Int], base: Int where _ >= 2) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc:
The number with these digits in `base`, most significant first, or `none` if a digit is
outside `0 .. base` or the value overflows. `from_digits([], b) == some(0)`.

api.name: to_radix
api.sig: fn to_radix(n: Int, base: Int where _ >= 2 and _ <= 36) -> Str
api.doc:
`n` written in `base` 2 to 36 with lowercase letters and a leading `-` when negative:
`to_radix(255, 16) == "ff"`, `to_radix(-5, 2) == "-101"`.

api.name: from_radix
api.sig: fn from_radix(s: Str, base: Int where _ >= 2 and _ <= 36) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc:
Parses `s` as an Int in `base` 2 to 36: an optional `+` or `-`, then one or more digits in
either case. No spaces, prefixes or separators. `none` on anything else or on overflow.

api.name: Rounding
api.sig: pub type Rounding = HalfUp | HalfDown | HalfEven | HalfAwayFromZero | HalfTowardZero | Up | Down | Ceiling | Floor derive Eq, Show

api.name: div_round
api.sig: fn div_round(a: Int, b: Int where _ != 0, mode: Rounding) -> Int
api.doc:
`a / b` rounded to an Int with `mode` (the exact quotient decides, with no overflow in the
comparison): `div_round(7, 2, HalfEven) == 4`, `div_round(-7, 2, Floor) == -4`.
Traps on `int_min() / -1`, like `/`.

api.name: round_int_to_multiple
api.sig: fn round_int_to_multiple(n: Int, step: Int where _ > 0, mode: Rounding) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc:
`n` rounded to a multiple of `step` with `mode`, or `none` if that multiple overflows:
`round_int_to_multiple(17, 5, HalfEven) == some(15)`.

api.name: round_to
api.sig: fn round_to(x: F64, places: Int where _ >= -400 and _ <= 400, mode: Rounding) -> F64
api.doc:
`x` rounded to `places` decimal places (negative `places` round to tens, hundreds, ...) with
`mode`. The rounding is exact on the shortest decimal that prints as `x` (its `.str`), so
`round_to(2.675, 2, HalfAwayFromZero) == 2.68` even though the binary double is slightly
below 2.675; the result is the double nearest to the rounded decimal. NaN, infinities and
zeros come back unchanged, and a value already short enough is returned as it is.

api.name: round_to_multiple
api.sig: fn round_to_multiple(x: F64, step: F64 where _ > 0.0, mode: Rounding) -> F64
api.doc:
`x` rounded to a multiple of `step` with `mode`: `round_to_multiple(7.3, 0.5, HalfEven) == 7.5`.
Like `round_to`, it works exactly on the shortest decimals that print as `x` and `step`, so
`round_to_multiple(0.3, 0.1, Floor) == 0.3` (where `(0.3 / 0.1).floor` is 2), and returns the
double nearest the exact multiple. NaN and infinities come back unchanged; a multiple too
large for F64 is an infinity.

api.name: lerp
api.sig: fn lerp(a: F64, b: F64, t: F64) -> F64
api.doc:
The value `t` of the way from `a` to `b`: `a` at 0, `b` at 1, extrapolating outside
(`lerp(10.0, 20.0, 0.25) == 12.5`). Exact at both ends.

api.name: inverse_lerp
api.sig: fn inverse_lerp(a: F64, b: F64, v: F64) -> Opt[F64]
api.doc: Where `v` lies between `a` and `b` (0 at `a`, 1 at `b`), or `none` when `a == b`.

api.name: remap
api.sig: fn remap(v: F64, in_lo: F64, in_hi: F64, out_lo: F64, out_hi: F64) -> Opt[F64]
api.doc:
`v` mapped linearly from the range `in_lo .. in_hi` to `out_lo .. out_hi` (not clamped), or
`none` when the input range is empty.

api.name: smoothstep
api.sig: fn smoothstep(edge0: F64, edge1: F64, x: F64) -> F64
api.doc:
The smooth Hermite step from 0 at `edge0` to 1 at `edge1` (GLSL `smoothstep`), clamped to
0 and 1 outside; when the edges are equal it is a hard step at `edge0`.

api.name: approx_equal
api.sig: fn approx_equal(a: F64, b: F64, rel_tol: F64 where _ >= 0.0, abs_tol: F64 where _ >= 0.0) -> Bool
api.doc:
Whether `a` and `b` are close, as Python's `math.isclose`: `|a - b| <= max(rel_tol *
max(|a|, |b|), abs_tol)`. NaN is close to nothing (not even NaN), an infinity only to itself,
and 0.0 and -0.0 are close. Use an `abs_tol` above 0 to compare with zero.

api.name: is_close
api.sig: fn is_close(a: F64, b: F64) -> Bool
api.doc: `approx_equal(a, b, 1e-9, 0.0)`, Python's default.

api.name: deg_to_rad
api.doc: Degrees to radians.

api.name: rad_to_deg
api.doc: Radians to degrees.

api.name: wrap
api.sig: fn wrap(x: F64, lo: F64, hi: F64) -> F64
api.doc:
`x` wrapped into the half-open range `lo .. hi`, as an angle or a ring buffer index would
wrap: `wrap(370.0, 0.0, 360.0) == 10.0`, `wrap(-1.0, 0.0, 360.0) == 359.0`. NaN and the
infinities give NaN.

api.name: normalize_degrees
api.doc: An angle in degrees normalized to `0 .. 360`.

api.name: normalize_radians
api.doc: An angle in radians normalized to `-pi .. pi`.

api.name: is_prime
api.doc:
Whether `n` is prime. Deterministic for every Int: trial division by the primes below 40,
then Miller-Rabin with the first twelve prime bases, which has no false positives below
3.3 * 10^24.

api.name: primes_up_to
api.sig: fn primes_up_to(limit: Int where _ >= 0 and _ <= 10000000) -> List[Int]
api.doc:
Every prime up to and including `limit`, in order, by the sieve of Eratosthenes. The limit is
capped at 10,000,000 (664,579 primes) to keep the memory bounded.

api.name: next_prime
api.doc:
The smallest prime greater than `n`, or `none` when that is above `int_max()`
(the largest Int prime is 9223372036854775783).

api.name: prev_prime
api.doc: The largest prime less than `n`, or `none` when `n <= 2`.

api.name: prime_factors
api.doc:
The prime factors of `n` with multiplicity, in increasing order: `prime_factors(360) ==
[2, 2, 2, 3, 3, 5]`, `prime_factors(1) == []`. Trial division by the primes below 1000, then
Pollard's rho (with Miller-Rabin to stop), so any Int factors in well under a second natively.

api.name: factorize
api.sig: fn factorize(n: Int where _ >= 1) -> List[(Int, Int)]
api.doc:
The factorization of `n` as `(prime, exponent)` pairs in increasing order of prime:
`factorize(360) == [(2, 3), (3, 2), (5, 1)]`, `factorize(1) == []`.

api.name: divisors
api.doc: Every positive divisor of `n`, in increasing order: `divisors(12) == [1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12]`.

api.name: totient
api.doc: Euler's totient: how many of `1 ..= n` are coprime to `n`.

api.name: factorial
api.sig: fn factorial(n: Int where _ >= 0 and _ <= 100000) -> BigInt
api.doc: `n!`, exactly. `n` is capped at 100,000 (456,574 digits).

api.name: factorial_int
api.doc: `n!` as an Int, or `none` above 20!.

api.name: comb
api.sig: fn comb(n: Int where _ >= 0, k: Int) -> BigInt
api.doc:
The binomial coefficient "n choose k", exactly: 0 when `k < 0` or `k > n`. Takes
`min(k, n - k)` BigInt steps.

api.name: comb_int
api.sig: fn comb_int(n: Int where _ >= 0, k: Int) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc: "n choose k" as an Int, or `none` if it overflows; 0 when `k < 0` or `k > n`.

api.name: perm
api.sig: fn perm(n: Int where _ >= 0, k: Int) -> BigInt
api.doc:
The number of ordered arrangements of `k` items out of `n`, `n! / (n - k)!`, exactly;
0 when `k < 0` or `k > n`.

api.name: perm_int
api.sig: fn perm_int(n: Int where _ >= 0, k: Int) -> Opt[Int]
api.doc: `perm(n, k)` as an Int, or `none` if it overflows.

api.name: multinomial
api.sig: fn multinomial(ks: List[Int] where _.all(k => k >= 0)) -> BigInt
api.doc: The multinomial coefficient `(k1 + k2 + ...)! / (k1! k2! ...)`, exactly; 1 for an empty list.

api.name: catalan
api.doc: The `n`th Catalan number, `comb(2n, n) / (n + 1)`: 1, 1, 2, 5, 14, 42, ...

api.name: fibonacci
api.doc: The `n`th Fibonacci number (F(0) = 0, F(1) = 1), exactly, by fast doubling.

api.name: fibonacci_int
api.doc: The `n`th Fibonacci number as an Int, or `none` above F(92).

api.name: floats
api.doc: The Int list as F64s, to feed the statistics functions.

api.name: checked_sum
api.doc: The sum of `xs`, or `none` if it overflows (the builtin `sum` traps instead).

api.name: checked_product
api.doc: The product of `xs` (1 for an empty list), or `none` if it overflows.

api.name: compensated_sum
api.doc:
The sum of `xs` with Neumaier's compensated summation, which keeps the rounding error of
long or cancelling sums near one ulp: `compensated_sum([1e100, 1.0, -1e100]) == 1.0` where
`sum` gives 0.0. Infinities and NaN give what a plain sum gives. 0.0 for an empty list.

api.name: product
api.doc: The product of `xs` (1.0 for an empty list).

api.name: cumulative_sum
api.doc: The running compensated sums: `cumulative_sum([1.0, 2.0, 3.0]) == [1.0, 3.0, 6.0]`.

api.name: mean
api.doc:
The arithmetic mean, or `none` for an empty list. Uses the compensated sum, and rescales
when the sum of finite values would overflow, so `mean([1e308, 1e308]) == some(1e308)`.

api.name: weighted_mean
api.sig: fn weighted_mean(xs: List[F64], ws: List[F64]) -> Opt[F64]
api.doc:
The mean of `xs` weighted by `ws`, or `none` if the lengths differ, the list is empty, a
weight is negative or the weights sum to 0.

api.name: geometric_mean
api.doc: The geometric mean, or `none` for an empty list or a negative value; 0.0 if any value is 0.

api.name: harmonic_mean
api.doc:
The harmonic mean, or `none` for an empty list or a negative value; 0.0 if any value is 0
(as Python's `statistics.harmonic_mean`).

api.name: median
api.doc: The median (the mean of the two middle values for an even count), or `none` for an empty list.

api.name: median_low
api.doc: The lower of the two middle values (the middle one for an odd count), or `none` if empty.

api.name: median_high
api.doc: The higher of the two middle values (the middle one for an odd count), or `none` if empty.

api.name: mode
api.doc:
The most common value, the first one seen on ties, or `none` for an empty list. Works for any
type; values compare with `==` (so NaN counts as equal to NaN).

api.name: multimode
api.doc: Every most common value, in first-seen order; `[]` for an empty list.

api.name: pvariance
api.doc: The population variance (divided by n), or `none` for an empty list. Welford's algorithm.

api.name: variance
api.doc: The sample variance (divided by n - 1), or `none` for fewer than two values.

api.name: pstdev
api.doc: The population standard deviation, or `none` for an empty list.

api.name: stdev
api.doc: The sample standard deviation, or `none` for fewer than two values.

api.name: Quantile
api.sig: pub type Quantile = Linear | Exclusive | Lower | Higher | Midpoint | Nearest | NearestRank derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
How a quantile is read off the sorted data (`h` is the 0-based position `(n - 1) * p`):
`Linear` interpolates at `h` (R-7, the default of NumPy, Excel PERCENTILE.INC and Python's
`method="inclusive"`); `Exclusive` interpolates at `(n + 1) * p - 1`, clamped to the data
(R-6, Python's default `method="exclusive"`, Excel PERCENTILE.EXC); `Lower` and `Higher` take
the element at `floor(h)` or `ceil(h)`; `Midpoint` averages those two; `Nearest` takes the
element nearest `h`, ties to even (NumPy's "nearest"); `NearestRank` takes the element at rank
`ceil(p * n)` (the classical nearest-rank method, never interpolated).

api.name: quantile
api.sig: fn quantile(xs: List[F64], p: F64 where _ >= 0.0 and _ <= 1.0, method: Quantile) -> Opt[F64]
api.doc:
The `p` quantile (0 to 1) of `xs` by `method`, or `none` for an empty list; NaN if `xs`
holds a NaN. `quantile(xs, 0.5, Linear)` is the median.

api.name: percentile
api.sig: fn percentile(xs: List[F64], p: F64 where _ >= 0.0 and _ <= 100.0) -> Opt[F64]
api.doc: The `p` percentile (0 to 100) with linear interpolation (`Linear`), or `none` if empty.

api.name: quantiles
api.sig: fn quantiles(xs: List[F64], n: Int where _ >= 1, method: Quantile) -> Opt[List[F64]]
api.doc:
The `n - 1` cut points that divide `xs` into `n` groups of equal probability, as Python's
`statistics.quantiles(xs, n=n, method=...)` (pass `Exclusive` for its default): `n = 4` gives
the quartiles. `none` for an empty list.

api.name: iqr
api.doc: The interquartile range, Q3 - Q1 with `Linear` quantiles, or `none` for an empty list.

api.name: value_range
api.doc: The largest value minus the smallest, or `none` for an empty list.

api.name: zscores
api.doc:
The z-score of each value, `(x - mean) / pstdev`, or `none` for an empty list or one whose
values are all equal.

api.name: min_max_normalize
api.doc:
Each value scaled to `0 .. 1` by `(x - min) / (max - min)`, or `none` for an empty list or
one whose values are all equal.

api.name: covariance
api.sig: fn covariance(xs: List[F64], ys: List[F64]) -> Opt[F64]
api.doc:
The sample covariance (divided by n - 1), as Python's `statistics.covariance`, or `none` if
the lengths differ or there are fewer than two pairs.

api.name: correlation
api.sig: fn correlation(xs: List[F64], ys: List[F64]) -> Opt[F64]
api.doc:
Pearson's correlation coefficient in -1 to 1, or `none` if the lengths differ, there are
fewer than two pairs, or either series is constant.

api.name: ranks
api.doc:
The rank of each value, 1 for the smallest, with ties given the average of their ranks
(`ranks([10.0, 20.0, 10.0]) == [1.5, 3.0, 1.5]`), as used by Spearman's correlation.

api.name: spearman
api.sig: fn spearman(xs: List[F64], ys: List[F64]) -> Opt[F64]
api.doc:
Spearman's rank correlation (Pearson's on the ranks, ties averaged), or `none` as for
`correlation`.

api.name: Fit
api.sig: pub type Fit = {slope: F64, intercept: F64, r_squared: F64} derive Eq, Show
api.doc:
The least squares line through a set of points: `y = slope * x + intercept`, and `r_squared`,
the share of the variance in `y` it explains (1.0 when `y` is constant and the fit is exact).

api.name: linear_regression
api.sig: fn linear_regression(xs: List[F64], ys: List[F64]) -> Opt[Fit]
api.doc:
Simple linear regression of `ys` on `xs` by ordinary least squares, or `none` if the lengths
differ, there are fewer than two points, or every `x` is the same.

api.name: Bin
api.sig: pub type Bin = {lo: F64, hi: F64, count: Int} derive Eq, Show
api.doc: One histogram bin: the values `v` with `lo <= v < hi` (the last bin also takes `hi`).

api.name: histogram_range
api.sig: fn histogram_range(xs: List[F64], lo: F64, hi: F64, bins: Int where _ >= 1) -> List[Bin]
api.doc:
`bins` equal-width bins from `lo` to `hi`, counting the values of `xs` inside that range;
values outside it and NaN are not counted.

api.name: histogram
api.sig: fn histogram(xs: List[F64], bins: Int where _ >= 1) -> List[Bin]
api.doc:
`bins` equal-width bins spanning the smallest to the largest finite value of `xs`; `[]` when
there is none. When every value is the same, one bin `[v, v]` holds them all.

api.name: moving_average
api.sig: fn moving_average(xs: List[F64], window: Int where _ >= 1) -> List[F64]
api.doc:
The trailing simple moving average over `window` values: one result per full window, so
`xs.len - window + 1` results (`[]` when `xs` is shorter than the window).

api.name: exponential_moving_average
api.sig: fn exponential_moving_average(xs: List[F64], alpha: F64 where _ > 0.0 and _ <= 1.0) -> List[F64]
api.doc:
The exponential moving average with smoothing factor `alpha` (0 < alpha <= 1), seeded with
the first value: `e[0] = x[0]`, `e[i] = alpha * x[i] + (1 - alpha) * e[i - 1]`.
